analysis.one_liner: Hyundai Motor India manufactures and sells passenger vehicles, SUVs and EVs in India and exports them from its Chennai plant, as the India-listed arm of Korea's Hyundai Motor Company.
analysis.whats_happening: Hyundai Motor India reported Q2 FY27 results on October 28, 2026 - just three days ago. Consolidated revenue crossed ₹20,000 crore for the first time (₹20,696 crore, up 18.5% YoY) on record volumes of 219,072 units, but EBITDA margin fell to 9.5% from 13.9% a year earlier on raw-material cost inflation, and net profit fell 23.9% YoY to about ₹1,196 crore. The stock reportedly rose after the print as investors focused on the volume record and management's reiterated full-year margin guidance rather than the profit decline.
analysis.plain_terms: Hyundai sold more cars than ever this quarter, but kept less profit out of every rupee of revenue than it did a year ago because raw material costs rose faster than prices - that is a margin story, not a demand problem. The business is genuinely growing in volume while profitability lags behind it, and management is promising the gap closes in the second half. The tension to watch: the stock already trades at a premium multiple that assumes that promise comes true.
analysis.quarters: Q2 FY27 (quarter ended Sept 2026, reported Oct 28, 2026): consolidated revenue ₹20,696 crore, up 18.5% YoY - the company's first quarter above ₹20,000 crore. Volumes were 219,072 units, up 14.7% YoY and 23% QoQ, led by SUVs and exports. EBITDA margin compressed to 9.5% from 13.9% a year earlier - management attributed roughly 400 basis points of this to commodity/raw-material cost inflation plus higher employee costs. Consolidated net profit fell 23.9% YoY to about ₹1,196 crore (standalone profit ₹1,189 crore, down 24%). No tax or revenue-recognition reclassification was flagged by the company this quarter, so the margin fall looks like a genuine cost story rather than an accounting artifact. Management held full-year EBITDA margin guidance at 11-14%, saying H2 margin needs to run slightly above 12% to hit roughly the 11% full-year mark, citing a Tamil Nadu incentive, export growth, price hikes, and new launches (Bayon, a dedicated EV) as the levers for recovery.
analysis.performance_read: The stock is down 31.3% from its September 2025 peak of ₹2,782.73, last at ₹1,911, inside a 52-week range of ₹1,675-2,415. There are no stock splits, bonus issues, or demergers in the corporate-action record, so this is a plain price decline - not a case where a spin-off understates returns. That said, the company has only been listed since October 2024 (about 2 years), so there is no meaningful long-term track record to draw conclusions from. The reported 'all-time' return of +7.05% versus the Nifty's -5.8% largely reflects a weak IPO-era entry price rather than demonstrated multi-year compounding; over 1 year the stock has lagged the Nifty (-20.1% vs -10.9%), while over 6 months it has outperformed (+4.6% vs -4.4%).
analysis.valuation_read: The stock trades around 33-34x trailing earnings per the most commonly cited figures, versus a broader auto-sector average closer to 27x - though different data providers show meaningfully different P/E figures (some as low as ~24-28x) depending on which trailing period and share count they use, so treat the exact multiple with some caution. It is expensive relative to a quarter in which profit just fell 24% YoY - the premium is being paid for an expected margin recovery and export/SUV mix improvement, not current earnings. Why it might deserve a premium: ROE near 30% and ROCE near 38% both sit well above sector medians, and the balance sheet carries no net debt. Whether that premium is justified hinges entirely on whether H2 margins actually land in management's guided 11-14% range.
analysis.growth_read: This is volume-led growth running into a margin squeeze, not a margin illusion over flat volumes. Q2 FY27 revenue grew 18.5% YoY and units sold grew 14.7% YoY to a record 219,072 - genuine demand growth, backed by record SUV mix and strong exports. But EBITDA margin fell about 440 basis points YoY to 9.5%, so profit growth is lagging volume growth for now. The business is expanding; profitability has not kept pace this quarter.
analysis.health_read: Profits are converting to cash reasonably well - FY26 operating cash flow was about ₹7,321 crore against free cash flow of about ₹2,996 crore. As of March 2026 the company held about ₹10,042 crore of cash against only about ₹1,082 crore of debt, i.e. a net cash position. The present pressure is a business-risk issue - commodity cost inflation and pricing/mix - not a financial-risk one; there is no leverage or liquidity concern to worry about here.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoter Hyundai Motor Company (Korea) holds 82.5%, unchanged, with zero shares pledged. Free float is thin at roughly 2% public holding; mutual funds hold about 8% (rising through 2026) and other domestic institutions hold the bulk of the remainder, while FII holding has fallen sharply across 2026 - from about 6.4% in December 2025 to roughly 3.2% in September 2026, a notable run of foreign-investor selling. No globally known value investor appears on the shareholder register - this is an institution- and promoter-held stock rather than one with marquee individual backing. Worth flagging structurally: the October 2024 listing was entirely an offer-for-sale by the Korean parent, so no fresh capital came into the company itself at IPO.
strengths: Record quarterly revenue of ₹20,696 crore in Q2 FY27, up 18.5% YoY - first quarter ever above ₹20,000 crore.
ROE near 30% and ROCE near 38%, both comfortably above sector medians.
Net cash balance sheet: about ₹10,042 crore cash versus about ₹1,082 crore debt as of March 2026.
Record volumes of 219,072 units in the quarter, up 14.7% YoY, led by a highest-ever SUV mix and strong export growth.
watchpoints: EBITDA margin fell to 9.5% from 13.9% YoY in Q2 FY27 - management must claw back roughly 400bps to meet its own 11-14% full-year guidance.
Consolidated net profit fell 23.9% YoY to about ₹1,196 crore even as revenue grew - profit growth is lagging volume growth.
FII holding has dropped from about 6.4% to about 3.2% of the register through 2026 - sustained foreign-investor selling.
Stock is 31.3% below its September 2025 peak with only about 2 years of trading history - too short to judge a genuine long-term track record either way.
analysis.one_thing: Whether H2 FY27 EBITDA margin actually climbs above the roughly 12% level management says is needed to hit its full-year 11-14% guidance - that single data point will show whether the current cost pressure is temporary or a structural reset in profitability.
analysis.data_notes: Q2 FY27 revenue, volume, EBITDA margin and net profit figures are cross-checked across multiple independent reports (Business Standard, Business Upturn, GuruFocus/Yahoo earnings-call highlights) and agree closely. P/E figures diverge meaningfully across sources (roughly 24x to 34x depending on provider and period) - treat the exact multiple as indicative, not precise; Screener's ~33.9x was used as the primary reference given consistency with ROE/ROCE figures from the same source. Shareholding and pledge data (82.5% promoter, 0% pledge) is consistent across sources. FY26 debt and cash-flow figures are from aggregator sites (Alpha Spread, stockanalysis.com) and were not cross-checked against the company's own annual report - treat as reasonably reliable but not primary-source verified. No upcoming results date or record date falls within the next two weeks as of October 31, 2026; the most recent dividend (₹21, paid August 2026) is already reflected in the supplied data.
